items.title: DeFranco Buddy — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I had played Charlie Barnet and Gene Krupa, and Ted Fiorito, and a few other bands, territory bands.

ctx.x: Even less often that it would actually come to fruition, that’s amazing.

Typical of Dorsey. He was an interesting person, he was a marvelous trombonist, one of the best I ever heard. Strict band leader. But he was bigger than life, it was frightening, very intimidating. I sat down even to audition for his big band many years later. I had played Charlie Barnet and Gene Krupa, and Ted Fiorito, and a few other bands, territory bands. I sat down and they had these chairs lined up for the sax section, and a rhythm there section set up. And in came a pianist, I forgot his name now, anyway.…
That’s amazing that he remembered. Did someone tip him off do you think?

items.title: Buddy DeFranco interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 13, 1996
items.q: Scat Davis, Krupa, Charlie Barnet, Ted Fio Rito, and Boyd Raeburn.

ctx.x: So the first couple of bands, Krupa—
Scat Davis, Krupa, Charlie Barnet, Ted Fio Rito, and Boyd Raeburn. I don’t know if you ever heard Boyd Raeburn.
